title: The matrix-unit corner tensor map embeds and its quotient is killed by the corner
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $V$ be a $K$-vector space with an algebraic basis $(b_j)_{j\in J}$ (each vector has a unique finite expansion), and choose $j_0\in J$. Write $\lambda_j:V\to K$ for the coordinate functions and $E_{ij}(v)=\lambda_j(v)b_i$. Let $D\subseteq\operatorname{End}_K(V)$ be a unital $K$-subalgebra containing every $E_{ij}$; multiplication is composition. For $v\in V$ put $\theta_v(w)=\lambda_{j_0}(w)v$, and put $e=E_{j_0j_0}$. For every unital left $D$-module $H$, with its $K$-action induced by the scalar operators, $eH=\{eh:h\in H\}$ is a $K$-subspace, all $\theta_v$ belong to $D$, and the specified map
$$\Phi:V\otimes_K eH\longrightarrow H,\qquad v\otimes h\longmapsto\theta_vh$$
is a well-defined injective $K$-linear map satisfying $\Phi(Tz)=T\Phi(z)$ for $T\in D$, where $T$ acts on the first tensor factor. Its image $N$ is a $D$-submodule, and on the quotient $Q=H/N$ the operators $e$ and every $E_{jj}$ act as zero. The tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is algebraic, and no countability, topology or finite-dimensionality hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For any indices, evaluation on $w\in V$ gives $E_{ij}E_{kl}(w)=\lambda_l(w)\lambda_j(b_k)b_i=\delta_{jk}E_{il}(w)$. Thus $e^2=e$. Scalar operators commute with every $K$-linear operator, so the action of every element of $D$ on $H$ is $K$-linear for the specified restricted scalar action.

proof.text: The range $eH$ is a $K$-subspace: $eh+eh\prime=e(h+h\prime)$ and $a(eh)=e(ah)$. Also $e(eh)=eh$. Write $v=\sum_{i\in F}a_i b_i$ with $F$ finite. Then $\theta_v=\sum_{i\in F}a_iE_{ij_0}\in D$, since both sides send $w$ to $\lambda_{j_0}(w)v$. In particular $\theta_{b_j}=E_{jj_0}$ and $\theta_{b_{j_0}}=e$.

proof.text: The identities $\theta_{v+v\prime}=\theta_v+\theta_{v\prime}$ and $\theta_{av}=a\theta_v$, together with the linearity of the $D$-action on $H$, make $(v,h)\mapsto\theta_vh$ a $K$-bilinear map $V\times eH\to H$. The tensor universal property gives the unique $K$-linear map $\Phi:V\otimes_K eH\to H$ with the required pure-tensor formula.

proof.text: For $T\in D$, the first-factor action $T\otimes\mathrm{id}_{eH}$ is supplied by the tensor-product definition. These maps form a unital $D$-action by its linearity and composition clauses. Direct evaluation gives $T\theta_v=\theta_{Tv}$, hence $\Phi(Tv\otimes h)=\theta_{Tv}h=T\theta_vh=T\Phi(v\otimes h)$. The two $K$-linear maps agree on pure tensors, so tensor-Hom uniqueness gives $\Phi(Tz)=T\Phi(z)$ for every $z$.

proof.text: Pure tensors generate the algebraic tensor product. Absorbing scalar coefficients in the second factor, write $z=\sum_{r=1}^n v_r\otimes h_r$. Expand $v_r=\sum_{j\in F_r}a_{rj}b_j$ in the given algebraic basis. Bilinearity and finite regrouping give $z=\sum_{j\in F}b_j\otimes k_j$, where $F=\bigcup_r F_r$ and $k_j=\sum_r a_{rj}h_r\in eH$ (put $a_{rj}=0$ off $F_r$). All sums here are finite.

proof.text: If $\Phi(z)=0$, the preceding expansion gives $\sum_{j\in F}E_{jj_0}k_j=0$ in $H$. For each $k\in F$ act by $E_{j_0k}$. The matrix-unit identity in step 1 reduces the sum to $e k_k=k_k$, since $k_k\in eH$. Thus every coefficient is zero and $z=0$. Applying this to $z-z\prime$ proves injectivity of $\Phi$.

proof.text: The image $N$ of the linear map $\Phi$ is closed under sums and negatives; step 4 gives $T\Phi(z)=\Phi(Tz)\in N$, so it is a $D$-submodule and the induced action on $Q=H/N$ is well defined. For $h\in H$, $eh\in eH$ and $\Phi(b_{j_0}\otimes eh)=e(eh)=eh$, so $e$ kills every class in $Q$. Finally $E_{jj}=E_{jj_0}eE_{j_0j}$, by step 1; acting on $Q$ shows that every $E_{jj}$ kills $Q$ as well. No infinite sum or restriction on the cardinality of $J$ or $H$ was used.

Step 1: E_ij E_kl = δ_jk E_il with composition as multiplication, and scalar operators are central. Step 2: θ_v = Σ a_i E_{i j0} is a finite sum, so θ_v lies in D, and eH is a subspace fixed by e. Step 3: the map is bilinear and the tensor universal property, as the cited node states it, gives Φ. Step 4: T⊗id is the node's f⊗id with its linearity, identity and composition clauses. Tθ_v = θ_{Tv}, and the last sentence of lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-currying gives equality from agreement on pure tensors. Step 5: pure tensors generate, so z = Σ b_j⊗k_j with k_j in eH. Step 6: acting by E_{j0 k} isolates e k_k = k_k, so Φ is injective. Step 7: N is D-stable, e kills Q because Φ(b_{j0}⊗eh) = eh, and E_jj = E_{j j0} e E_{j0 j} then kills Q too. Small cases: for H = V, Φ is an isomorphism and Q = 0. For H = D = End(V) with J infinite, Q is nonzero but killed by every E_jj, so the statement does not claim surjectivity. |J| = 1 and H = 0 are trivial.
